headline: HMC Capital CEO Sid Sharma bullish on HomeCo REIT outlook despite FY27 FFO dip driven by interest rate headwinds
reasoning: Sharma describes FY26 as a year of disciplined operational excellence, with FFO of $0.09 per unit and distributions of 8.6 cents, both in line with guidance. He acknowledges a moderate 2% dip in FFO to 8.8 cents in FY27 driven by higher financing costs, noting the trust has absorbed the interest rate headwind upfront. Despite this, he is bullish on the operational outlook, citing strong tenant sales, rising foot traffic, and no observable correlation between consumer sentiment and consumer spending. He notes July and August trading has been remarkably stronger than Q3 and Q4 of FY26, and expects retailers to outperform consensus expectations over the next six months. Rental growth is expected to remain predictable and growing, underpinned by structural undersupply of high-quality retail space and occupancy running well in excess of 99% across the sector. The trust may selectively divest one or two assets trading inside cost of debt, which could be earnings accretive.
quote: No. 2026 was just another year of disciplined operational excellence. Our centers are performing well. More importantly, our retailers are performing well. So we've delivered on our guidance for FY 26 of $0.09 per unit. I suppose with with everyone else in the real estate sector, what's in front of us? There's some interest expense headwinds in FY 27. So our guidance next year or sorry, this year compared to 26 shows a moderate, uh, moderate pullback on the FFO per unit from $0.09 to 8.8 cents. Um, but really, what's happening in the assets is still quite remarkable. Um, the consumers are spending and there's no correlation really, that we can see between consumer sentiment and consumer spending. So tenant sales are up. Expenditures are foot traffic's up. Um, so we're actually, you know, pretty bullish about the outlook this year.

headline: Holds but is personally uninterested, noting an 18% NTA discount is not compelling enough for 15-20% returns
reasoning: Coleman questions why a wealthy Australian with existing property exposure would want further equity exposure through a REIT. For REIT investors, the relevant metrics are yield and NTA discount. Homeco trades at an 18% discount to NTA, which is interesting but insufficient to generate 15-20% annual returns. NTA growth of a couple of percent per year plus a small yield is only attractive to those seeking single-digit returns with professional property management.
quote: If you do want to be inside REITs, the question you should always be asking is what's the yield and what's the NTA? Because at the end of the day, that's why you're there... in the case of Homeco, you know, Daily Needs REIT, they are currently trading on about an 18% discount to their NTA. So if you like the space, you'd have to ask, is an 18% discount enough to entice you to part with your money for their shares? And do you think that that NTA will continue to grow at or above inflation so that your yield continues to grow at or above inflation? Now, if you're wanting 15% to 20% per annum, that's very hard to get when your only elements that you can put in there is a small discount to NTA and a small yield.
